claims.statement: Shell ViewModels (PlayerViewModel, SettingsViewModel, AppMediaMetadataViewModel, PlaylistResumeViewModel, EmotionViewModel, MoodTimeSlotViewModel) must be created at AppRoot's Activity scope and passed into AppNavHost as parameters; calling viewModel() inside a NavHost composable block falls back to the non-Hilt SavedStateViewModelFactory and crashes for @HiltViewModel classes needing injected dependencies (regression recorded 2026-09-04 in source comments).

PlayerUiState.isLoading defaults to true so the first frame is a full-screen LoadingSplash; AppRoot returns before composing MusicplayerTheme, AppScaffold, AppNavHost, and the toast/queue overlays until startup loading completes, and error-message toasts (errorMessage → toast + clearError) are likewise gated behind loading.

SettingsViewModel exposes persisted StateFlows from PlayerSettingsRepository — themeMode (default SYSTEM), themeVariant (default MONO), lyricFontScale (default 1f), each stateIn(WhileSubscribed(5_000)) with write-through setters — and AppRoot derives isDarkTheme from themeMode (SYSTEM → isSystemInDarkTheme), wraps the shell in MusicplayerTheme(darkTheme, variant), and syncs status-bar icon appearance via WindowCompat.getInsetsController.

MusicplayerTheme resolves ThemeMode×ThemeVariant onto four ThemePalettes (mono-light, mono-dark with OLED #000000, vermilion-day, vermilion-night) via paletteToColorScheme (primary=accent, background/surface=bg0, outlineVariant=out1), matching the token tables in docs/ui-design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md; dynamic color is disabled by default and LocalContentColor is explicitly provided as onSurface so uncolored text follows the theme.

PermissionCoordinator.requestAudioFolderAccess launches the custom PersistableOpenDocumentTree contract, which adds FLAG_GRANT_PERSISTABLE_URI_PERMISSION plus read/write grants so the picked SAF tree URI survives app restarts; the resulting URI flows to onFolderSelected → playerViewModel.importFolder(uri) with a count-based toast.

requestNotificationPermission/requestBluetoothConnectPermission consult RuntimePermissionPolicy (POST_NOTIFICATIONS only on Tiramisu+, BLUETOOTH_CONNECT only on S+, each with a user-facing denied message); an already-granted permission runs onGranted immediately, otherwise exactly one pending RuntimePermissionRequest continuation is stashed and launched — grant resumes it, denial routes the spec's deniedMessage to the shared toast — and a null spec short-circuits to onGranted on older OS versions; RuntimePermissionPolicyTest pins both cutoffs and messages.

Settings wires permission grants to player features (Bluetooth → initializeBluetoothPlayback, notification → setPlaybackNotificationEnabled(true), each with a success toast), and both permission requests must be user-triggered from Settings rather than at startup — a rule enforced by verifyProductArchitecture checking that the player startup facade contains no Bluetooth initialization and SettingsScreen keeps the 蓝牙播放监听/申请蓝牙权限 controls.

The shell owns a single rememberToastHost rendered as top-center ToastHost plus AutoDismissToasts(2000ms) above the NavHost; ToastHostState.showToast keeps only the latest entry (clearing prior ones), so attribution toasts replace rather than queue.

Lucky-play and infinite-play starts attribute mood-slot selection through toasts built from playerViewModel.currentMoodSlotName() (已按「{slotName}」为你随机播放 / 已按「{slotName}」开启无限随机播放), implementing the design doc's §4.5 anti-'attribution difficulty' rule, and both actions settle the playlist source via playlistResumeViewModel.switchSource(null, …).

deleteSongWithToast runs PlayerViewModel.deleteSong on a shell coroutine scope because the call is suspending end-to-end: PlayerSongDeletionFacade → SongDeletionCoordinator → MusicRepository.deleteSong performs the SAF DocumentFile cross-process delete inside withContext(Dispatchers.IO) (M-3, review 2026-09-03) before removing the song from songs/playlists, persisting, and deleting its emotion rows, so the main thread is never blocked (no ANR); DeleteSongResult.Success/Failure map directly to toasts.

AppRoutes is the single route-constant table (18 destination routes including the HOME start destination and parameterized playlist/{id}, artist/{name}, album/{name}, version-comparison/{groupId}, song-top-list?period patterns); parameterized routes must be built through its helper functions, which Uri.encode arguments — call sites never concatenate route strings.

AppDestinations.fromRoute maps every sub-page to its owning bottom tab (USER: settings, playback stats and its sub-pages, song top list, emotion analysis, mood time slot; PLAYLIST: playlist detail, artist/album detail, version management/comparison, quick-skip; everything else incl. Home and lyrics → HOME), and this single mapping synchronizes bottom-bar highlight via LaunchedEffect(activeRoute), computes enter/exit transitions by comparing tab ordinals (same-tab → no transition; pop transitions disabled), and gates edge-swipe tab paging which is disabled on the lyrics route.

AppScaffold adapts at 600dp between a phone layout (content + MusicPlayerBottomBar mini-player shown when the current destination is not HOME and a song is loaded, plus a bottom text nav bar) and a wide layout (left 72dp TextNavRail + content), with text-only three-destination navigation being a deliberately kept difference from the design mock.

Bottom-tab destinations navigate with the state-preserving recipe popUpTo(startDestination){saveState=true} + launchSingleTop + restoreState=true, so per-tab back stacks and UI state survive tab switches.

Each :feature:* module exposes only XxxRoute (a public composable taking XxxRouteState + XxxRouteActions + callbacks) plus an internal XxxScreen; AppNavHost is the sole place routes are wired and cross-feature jumps happen — verifyProductArchitecture forbids feature-to-feature Gradle deps, requires Route/Screen pairs per feature, and fails the build if overlay-routing files (AppOverlayHost etc.) are reintroduced.

Route-state derivation (playlistRouteState, userRouteState, playStatsRouteState, playbackStatsRouteState, songTopListRouteState, resolveResumeSong, flatGroupedSongs) is concentrated in pure, side-effect-free functions in AppRouteStateMappers.kt (documented as independently testable), while navigation/playback action assembly lives in AppRouteActionMappers.kt, keeping AppNavHost down to route table plus transitions.

The O(n) grouped-and-flattened library is computed once at NavHost level (remember(uiState.songs) { flatGroupedSongs(...) }) and passed as precomputedLibrarySongs to playlist/stats/artist/album/version routes, eliminating per-recomposition regrouping on 1100+ song libraries (M-7 review); mappers fall back to internal computation only for legacy callers/tests.

positionMs (~500ms updates) and sleepTimerRemainingMs (1s ticks) are narrow StateFlows deliberately outside PlayerUiState so high-frequency ticks never recompose the whole shell (M-6 fix); only the destinations that need them subscribe — HomeRoute (position + sleep timer), LyricsRoute (position), VersionComparisonRoute (seek bar).

Every click-a-song action queues through PlayerViewModel.playWith(song, SongPlaybackStrategy): SongPlaybackStrategy.single() queues only the clicked song (stats pages, local-music single click, staying on the page), while scope(list) queues the displayed group (playlist/artist/album/top list/quick-skip/version group) in sequential mode starting from the clicked song, replacing any existing queue.

PlaylistResumeViewModel.switchSource(newSource, currentSongId) settles the previous playlist source inside a single repository transaction — the library page always settles with a null source on song click, playlist detail passes its id only when the clicked song belongs to it, and onResumePlaylist plays the resolved song then clears the banner; resolveResumeSong nulls stale records whose song left the playlist or is unplayable (uri == null), covered by ResolveResumeSongTest.

AppRoot provides LocalEmotionCorrectionController once above the scaffold, delegating save to AppMediaMetadataViewModel.saveEmotionCorrection (empty word set → clearCorrection to restore auto tags, requiring an existing row; otherwise EmotionGroup.avgOfWords resolves the words to V-A anchor coordinates for saveCorrection; repository bridges run on Dispatchers.Default), refreshing EmotionViewModel on success and toasting 这首歌还没完成分析 on failure — so any page rendering SongInfoDialog/SongEmotionSection gains the 不像？标记 capability without callback threading, and SongEmotionSection shows its calibrate button only when the controller is non-null.

The emotion-analysis page derives failed-song rows with a produceState keyed on the failure fingerprint + songs list + a local calibrationVersion; because manual marks do not change the failure record (attempts/failedAt unchanged), onCalibrateSong must increment calibrationVersion after a successful save to force a requery (2026-09-04 regression where the list only updated after leaving the page), and marking a failed song without an analysis row creates a user-only record through the shared controller.

MoodTimeSlotViewModel observes TimeSlotConfigRepository configs and the persisted moodTimeSlotEnabled switch; loadStats() computes tag→song counts and library size once per config-page entry on Dispatchers.IO (degrading badges to zero on failure), save() reports overlap/zero-length validation errors through a (Boolean, String?) callback surfaced as toasts, and MoodSlotEditDialog receives the tag counts plus the manual-only tag list (鬼畜/沙雕/戏谑/荒诞).

The player resolves the active mood slot from volatile moodSlotConfigsCache/moodEmotionTagsCache snapshots refreshed at startup (refreshMoodSlotCache) and falls back to full-library random when the tag-filtered pool is empty; the wiring seam MoodTimeSlotViewModel.onConfigsChanged and PlayerRuntime.refreshMoodSlots() exists for post-save cache refresh but currently has no caller, so config-page changes reach the player's random logic only at the next cold start.

Repository calls reached from composition (songInfo loading, playback-stats snapshots per review C-2, ranked counts) are wrapped in runCatching with safe defaults because the underlying Room runBlocking bridge throws; failures are logged via AppLog and degrade to null/EMPTY values instead of crashing the coroutine.

PlayerQueueSheetHost renders PlayQueueSheet above the scaffold, driven by shell-local showQueueSheet state with a BackHandler; selecting a song plays that queue index and dismisses the sheet, and removal/clear emit confirmation toasts.
